dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} . i 'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . thanks for coming in on short notice . what brings you here today ?
[patient] hi , doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . i 'm going to peru in november , and my travel agent said i need to see somebody about shots .
[doctor] okay . tell me about the trip . where are you going , and for how long ?
[patient] three weeks . we fly into lima , then go up to cusco and the sacred valley , and then take the train to machu picchu . my wife wants to do the four day trail , but i told her i 'd take the train .
[doctor] that 's a lot of altitude . have you ever been that high before ?
[patient] i went to denver once for a conference , and that 's a mile high . i was fine . cusco is over eleven thousand feet though . my brother in law , {OTHER_FIRST} , says he got sick there the first day .
[doctor] that 's very common . it 's worth planning for . do you take any medicines now ?
[patient] the lisinopril in the morning for my pressure , and a baby aspirin at night . nothing else .
[doctor] okay . do you remember your last tetanus shot ?
[patient] it was about eight years ago , at the riverbend pharmacy on elm street . i went in with my wife for a checkup and they gave it right there .
[doctor] good . so your tetanus is probably due . have you had any other vaccines ? hepatitis ? typhoid ?
[patient] i had the hepatitis b shots about ten years ago , when i worked at {ORG} . they tested my blood then . i think i 'm immune .
[doctor] okay . we 'll check the hepatitis titer to be sure . what kind of work did you do at {ORG} ?
[patient] i was an accountant there for thirty years . now i just do taxes part time for people in the neighborhood . a lot of it is seasonal .
[doctor] that 's a busy job . does anyone in your family have a bad reaction to vaccines ? anyone with a problem after a shot ?
[patient] my brother in law , {OTHER_FIRST} , had a bad reaction to something once . he swelled up pretty badly . that 's why he 's the one who got so sick at altitude . his doctor says he has parkinson 's now , poor guy .
[doctor] i 'm sorry to hear that . let me look at your blood pressure and your heart . your pressure today is one thirty six over eighty .
[patient] that 's better than last time . i 've been walking the dog every morning , trying to lose the weight .
[doctor] that 's great . any chest pain when you climb the hills ?
[patient] no , nothing like that . i get a little short of breath on the steep stairs at st. brendan 's , but that 's just being out of shape .
[doctor] okay . heart sounds are normal , no murmur . your lungs are clear . let 's check your legs . no swelling .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] for the trip , here is what i recommend . a tetanus booster now . the hepatitis a vaccine , two doses , and the typhoid vaccine is an option , oral or shot . plus a flu shot before you leave . and i want to talk about rabies , because you 'll be near animals .
[patient] rabies ? i 'm not going near any dogs there except maybe the stray ones .
[doctor] right . the rabies shots are for people who might be exposed , like hikers in the countryside . we can talk about it . i 'd like you to get the first dose of the hepatitis a today and come back in two weeks .
[patient] okay . can i get the other shots at the pharmacy ?
[doctor] yes , you can pick up the typhoid pills or the antibiotic for traveler 's diarrhea at the pharmacy , and bring the prescription .
[patient] i 'll take it to the pharmacy on elm street again .
[doctor] fine . and for altitude sickness , i 'd like to start acetazolamide two days before you go up to the high ground . it can make your fingers tingle , so tell me if that happens .
[patient] tingling , okay . my sister takes a pill for her ankles that makes her tingle too .
[doctor] okay . we 'll sort out your medicines with your sister 's doctor if needed . any questions ?
[patient] what about the washington guidelines ? my cousin said the government site says i need something special .
[doctor] the cdc travel guidance is the best source , not any one city . i 'll print the list for you .
[patient] thanks , doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . i 'll see you in two weeks .
[doctor] you 're welcome , {PATIENT_FIRST} . safe travels .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Pre-travel consultation for a three-week trip to high-altitude destinations in the Andes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male referred for pre-travel evaluation. He plans a three-week trip in November, flying into the capital and then traveling by train to a famous mountain citadel and the surrounding valley. He has previously traveled only to moderate altitude. His brother-in-law, {OTHER_FIRST}, developed altitude sickness on his first day at high elevation.

He reports a prior tetanus booster approximately eight years ago at Riverbend Pharmacy on Elm Street, and hepatitis B vaccination about ten years ago. He denies current symptoms and denies chest pain. He reports mild dyspnea on the steep stairs at St. Brendan's.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Retired accountant from {ORG}, now doing part-time tax preparation. He walks his dog every morning. He may hike in rural countryside but plans no visits to animal markets.

FAMILY HISTORY

Brother-in-law with Parkinson's disease and a prior severe reaction to a vaccine.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril daily and low-dose aspirin nightly.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Blood pressure 136/80. Heart sounds normal without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. No peripheral edema.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Pre-travel health counseling for high-altitude travel. Discussed acetazolamide prophylaxis to start two days before ascent, with counseling about paresthesias. Discussed rabies exposure risk in rural areas and pre-exposure prophylaxis options.

2. Immunizations today: hepatitis A dose 1, with dose 2 in two weeks. Typhoid vaccine offered. Influenza vaccine before departure.

3. Hypertension, controlled on current regimen. Continue.

4. Traveler's diarrhea prevention: prescribe an empiric antibiotic to carry, to be picked up at the pharmacy.

5. Hepatitis B immunity to be checked by serology.
